title: Interpreter of Maladies
subtitle: English quiz Mon, Nov 2
source: From the full text of the story by Jhumpa Lahiri (1999). Only details from the story itself.

sections.title: The characters

notes.key: Five people in one car: **Mr. Kapasi** the driver, and the Das family: **Mr. Das (Raj)**, **Mrs. Das (Mina)**, and their kids **Ronny, Bobby and Tina**.

list: 46 years old, silver receding hair, an unlined brow he dabs with **lotus-oil balm**.
Wears a tailored **gray** suit he designed for long hours driving. He's glad he chose the gray one and not the brown one that sags.
Gives tours on **Fridays and Saturdays only**. During the week he works in a **doctor's office as an interpreter** for **Gujarati** patients (his father was Gujarati).
He took that job after his **first son, age 7, got typhoid** and died. He used to teach English at a grammar school; the doctor paid twice as much.
As a young man he dreamed of being an **interpreter for diplomats and dignitaries**. Now he sees the job as a sign of his failings.
His marriage is cold and silent. His wife calls his job "doctor's assistant" and never asks about it.
**28 years old**. Wears a red and white checkered skirt, a shirt with a **strawberry** on it, and pink tinted **sunglasses** she rarely takes off.
Carries a big **straw bag**, eats **puffed rice** she shares with no one, paints her **nails** and won't paint Tina's.
Bored and detached from her husband and kids. She takes an interest only in Mr. Kapasi.
Teaches middle school **science** in **New Brunswick, New Jersey**.
Always behind his **camera** or reading his **tour book**. Talks about India like a tourist.
Does not know Bobby is not his son.
**Ronny**: the older boy, tries to give a goat gum.
**Bobby**: sits up front, is **not Raj's son**. His real father is a **Punjabi friend of Raj's** who stayed with them for a week and now lives in **London**. He gets attacked by monkeys at the end.
**Tina**: the little girl with a doll whose yellow hair is chopped off. She begs her mom to do her nails.

sections.title: What happens, in order

notes.p: One **Saturday in mid July**, Mr. Kapasi picks up the Das family at **Hotel Sandy Villa** to drive them to the **Sun Temple at Konarak**.

list: **1. Tea stall.** First stop because Tina needs the bathroom. The parents bicker over who takes her. Mrs. Das doesn't hold her hand.
**2. On the road.** The kids see monkeys. Mr. Das stops for photos, even of a starving man with bullocks. Mrs. Das complains there's no air conditioning.

**3. The reveal.** Mr. Kapasi says he works as an **interpreter** for a doctor. Mrs. Das calls it **"romantic"** and asks for stories about patients. He's flattered and starts checking himself in the mirror.
**4. Lunch.** Mrs. Das invites him to sit with them. Mr. Das has them lean in for a photo. She asks for his **address** so she can mail the pictures. He writes it on a scrap of her film magazine.

**5. Konarak.** The temple is shaped like a chariot with 24 carved wheels. His favorite statue is the **Astachala-Surya, the setting sun**. He fantasizes about writing letters with her and calculates he'll hear from her in **about six weeks**.
**6. The detour.** On the way back he suggests the hills at **Udayagiri and Khandagiri** just to keep the trip going. Mrs. Das stays in the car with him.
**7. The confession.** She tells him **Bobby isn't Raj's son** and that she's kept it secret for **eight years**. She wants him to interpret her feelings and give her a remedy.
**8. The question.** He asks, **"Is it really pain you feel, Mrs. Das, or is it guilt?"** She glares and walks off, spilling puffed rice.
**9. The monkeys.** The puffed rice draws monkeys to **Bobby**, who gets beaten with the stick he'd given one earlier. Mr. Kapasi scares them off and carries him back.
**10. The ending.** When Mrs. Das pulls out her hairbrush, the **slip with his address blows away** into the trees. Only Mr. Kapasi sees it.

notes.key: Arc in one line: flattered, then fantasizing, then disappointed. The confession kills his fantasy and the address blowing away ends it.

sections.title: Setting and cultural identity

notes.p: The story takes place in **Orissa, India** (near Puri), on a hot day in July.

list: Mr. and Mrs. Das are **Indian American**: "born and raised" in America. Their parents retired to **Assansol**, India, and they visit every couple of years.
They **look Indian but dress as foreigners did**: bright stiff clothes, caps with visors.
Mr. Das **squeezes hands like an American** instead of pressing palms together like Mr. Kapasi.
Mr. Das reads about India from a **tour book** and photographs poor locals like a tourist.
Mrs. Das doesn't understand the **Hindi love song** a man sings at her.
Mr. Kapasi knows America only from TV, like the show **Dallas**. Mr. Das says it went off the air.

notes.key: They are outsiders in both places: Indian by background, American in everything else. Kapasi treats them like any foreign tourists.

sections.title: Symbols

head: Symbol
What it means
rows: Kapasi's hope of a connection. It lands in her messy bag, then blows away: the fantasy is gone and she never cared.
Mrs. Das's selfishness. She never shares it, and her careless trail of it gets Bobby attacked.
Mr. Das sees India only through a lens and a guide. He's distant from the real place and his real family.
Mrs. Das hides behind them. She won't let anyone see her or connect.
Chaos the parents can't control. Kapasi says they're "more hungry than dangerous"; the danger comes from her carelessness.
Kapasi's favorite statue, tired after a day's work. Matches him and the end of his hope.
What Kapasi fixates on. It stands for the attraction he imagines.
The family is stuck together but closed off from each other.

notes.key: The biggest symbol is the address slip blowing away: the picture of the Das family Kapasi keeps forever is of them leaving his life.

sections.title: Themes

list: **Miscommunication and interpretation.** Kapasi translates symptoms for a living but can't read Mrs. Das. She wants him to interpret her feelings; he misreads her interest as romance. Nobody in the story really understands anybody.
**Loneliness and failed marriages.** Both marriages are empty: Kapasi's silent one and the Das's bickering one. Kapasi sees "the bickering, the indifference, the protracted silences" in both.
**Fantasy vs reality.** Kapasi builds a whole relationship in his head (letters, a photo in his Russian grammar). Reality: she only wanted a stranger to unload on.
**Parental neglect.** The parents act "like an older brother and sister, not parents." Nobody watches Bobby, and he gets hurt.
**Guilt vs pain.** Mrs. Das calls her feeling pain. Kapasi names it guilt. She can't face that.
**Cultural identity.** The Das family is Indian by background but American in every way, tourists in their parents' country.

notes.key: Title meaning: Kapasi interprets physical maladies for patients. Mrs. Das asks him to interpret her emotional malady, and he can't fix it.

sections.title: Key quotes

list: **"But so romantic"** (Mrs. Das on his job). The word that starts Kapasi's fantasy.
**"In a way, more dependent on you than the doctor"** (Mrs. Das). First time anyone treats his job as important.
**"The job was a sign of his failings."** How Kapasi really sees his life.
**"Mr. and Mrs. Das behaved like an older brother and sister, not parents."** Parental neglect.
**"Raj has his dumb book anyway."** Her contempt for her husband.
**"He's not his."** The confession about Bobby.
**"Is it really pain you feel, Mrs. Das, or is it guilt?"** Kapasi's question, the turning point.
**"he was not even important enough to be properly insulted"** Kapasi realizes he means nothing to her.

**"knowing that this was the picture of the Das family he would preserve forever in his mind"** The last line, as the address blows away.

sections.title: How to answer the 2 questions

notes.key: Every answer: **Claim** (answer the question in one sentence), **Quote** (exact words), **Explain** (what it shows), **Link** (tie it to a theme or the title).

notes.h: Likely question 1: how does the title connect to the story?

list: **Claim:** The title is ironic. Kapasi interprets physical maladies for a doctor, but he fails when Mrs. Das asks him to interpret her emotional one.
**Quote:** "I was hoping you could help me feel better, say the right thing. Suggest some kind of remedy."
**Explain:** She treats her guilt like a symptom he can translate. He can only ask "Is it really pain you feel, Mrs. Das, or is it guilt?", and she walks away.
**Link:** Miscommunication. Even a professional interpreter can't make two people understand each other.

notes.h: Likely question 2: how does Mr. Kapasi change?

list: **Claim:** He goes from flattered and hopeful to disappointed and alone again.
**Quote 1 (start):** "But so romantic" makes him feel important and starts his fantasy of letters with her.
**Quote 2 (end):** "he was not even important enough to be properly insulted", then the address slip blows away.
**Explain and link:** Fantasy vs reality. He returns to the same lonely life, keeping only the "picture of the Das family" in his mind.

notes.p: Other possible questions: what the puffed rice or the address slip symbolizes, how the Das parents treat their kids, or whether it's pain or guilt. Use the same four steps.

points: Answer the question directly in the first sentence (claim)
Use at least one exact quote
Explain what the quote shows
Link to a theme or the title
Title answer: he interprets physical maladies but fails with her emotional one
Change answer: flattered and hopeful, then disappointed and alone
